q: If the same residence renovation is instead contracted only for Detailed Architectural Design Services (DADS, 6% of PCC), what is the total Group IX (150%-of-RPF) DADS fee?
n: The Group IV DADS rate is a flat 6% of PCC: base RPF = 0.06 x P6,000,000 = P360,000.00. Applying the Sec. 6.3.9 150% increase: P360,000 x 1.5 = P540,000.00. Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.4 (Group IV DADS fee schedule) and Sec. 6.3.9
scenario: An architect is engaged to renovate an existing single-detached residence (a Group IV building). The PCC for the renovation is PHP 6,000,000.00.

q: Why does SPP Document 202 grant a higher (150% of RPF) fee for Group IX alteration/renovation work compared to ordinary new-construction work in the same base Group?
o: Because renovation projects are always larger in floor area than new buildings
Because renovation work is exempt from construction supervision duties
Because working within/around an existing structure typically demands extra investigation, coordination, and design effort beyond what a comparable new building requires
Because the Architect is required to hire additional consultants for every renovation project
n: The 50% premium recognizes that altering, renovating, rehabilitating, retrofitting, or expanding an existing building generally involves more complex site investigation, as-built verification, and design coordination than comparable new construction, justifying the higher compensation. Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.9

q: If the same monumental rehabilitation instead engages the architect only for DADS (7.5% of PCC), what is the total Group IX (150%-of-RPF) DADS fee?
n: The Group V DADS rate is a flat 7.5% of PCC: base RPF = 0.075 x P40,000,000 = P3,000,000.00. Applying the Sec. 6.3.9 150% increase: P3,000,000 x 1.5 = P4,500,000.00. Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.5 (Group V DADS fee schedule) and Sec. 6.3.9
scenario: An architect undertakes the restoration and rehabilitation of an existing monumental structure — a heritage mausoleum/memorial complex (a Group V – Monumental building). The PCC for the rehabilitation works is PHP 40,000,000.00.

q: A hospital (a Group III building) needs a new wing added to its existing structure. Which fee treatment applies to the Architect's Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services (DAEDS) for this addition?
o: The Group III DAEDS RPF schedule increased to 150%, since the hospital is an existing Group III building being expanded
The Group X hourly consultation rate
The Group III DAEDS RPF schedule at its ordinary (100%) rate, with no increase
The Group VIII (Extensive Detail) flat 15% rate
n: Because the hospital belongs to Group III (one of Groups 1-5) and the work is an expansion/addition to an existing building, Sec. 6.3.9 requires the ordinary Group III DAEDS RPF to be increased to a total of 150%. Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.9

q: What does 'DADS' stand for, as distinguished from DAEDS in the Group fee tables?
o: Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services
n: DADS refers to Detailed Architectural Design Services — the architectural-only design scope, billed at a lower RPF percentage than DAEDS (which also covers engineering design) for every Group. Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3 (Regular Design Services terminology)

q: Applying the Group IX rule to this renovation, what is the total (150%-of-RPF) DAEDS fee the architect may charge?
n: The base Group I DAEDS RPF is P900,000.00 (5% of P18M). Because this is a renovation of an existing Group I building, Sec. 6.3.9 increases this to 150%: P900,000 x 1.5 = P1,350,000.00. Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.9
scenario: An architect is engaged for the Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services (DAEDS) of the renovation of an existing warehouse (a Group I – Simple building). The Project Construction Cost (PCC) for the renovation is PHP 18,000,000.00.

q: What does 'PCC', the base figure multiplied by the RPF percentage in every fee computation, stand for?
n: PCC stands for Project Construction Cost — the base amount against which each Group's RPF percentage (and, for Group IX, the resulting 150% figure) is computed. Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3 (Regular Design Services terminology)

q: Before any Group IX adjustment, what is the ordinary (base) Group I DAEDS RPF for this project?
n: PCC of P120M falls in the 'Over P100M to P200M' tier: RPF = P4,500,000 + 3% of excess over P100M = P4,500,000 + (0.03 x P20,000,000) = P4,500,000 + P600,000 = P5,100,000.00. Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.1 (Group I DAEDS fee schedule)
scenario: An architect undertakes the DAEDS renovation and structural retrofit of an existing aircraft hangar (a Group I – Simple building). The PCC for the retrofit works is PHP 120,000,000.00.

q: By how much is the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) increased for Group IX (alteration/renovation) work, relative to the ordinary RPF for the same building's base Group?
o: Increased by twenty-five percent (25%), for a total of one hundred twenty-five percent (125%) of the RPF
Increased by one hundred percent (100%), for a total of two hundred percent (200%) of the RPF
Reduced by fifty percent (50%), for a total of fifty percent (50%) of the RPF
Increased by fifty percent (50%), for a total of one hundred fifty percent (150%) of the RPF
n: Sec. 6.3.9 states that for alteration/renovation/rehabilitation/retrofit/expansion work on existing buildings belonging to Groups 1 to 5, compensation is increased to fifty percent (50%) more, i.e. a total of one hundred fifty percent (150%) of the RPF. Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.9

q: What is the total Group IX (150%-of-RPF) DAEDS fee for this office-building expansion?
n: Since PCC (P20M) is P50M or less, the Group II DAEDS rate is a flat 6% of PCC: base RPF = 0.06 x P20,000,000 = P1,200,000.00. Because this is an expansion/addition to an existing Group II building, Sec. 6.3.9 increases this to 150%: P1,200,000 x 1.5 = P1,800,000.00. Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.2 (Group II DAEDS fee schedule) and Sec. 6.3.9
scenario: An architect is engaged for the DAEDS design of an expansion/addition to an existing office building (a Group II – Moderate building). The PCC for the expansion is PHP 20,000,000.00.

q: An architect is asked whether the Group IX 150%-of-RPF rule applies to the retrofit of an existing repetitive-construction housing project (a Group VII / Group VI type of building). What is the correct answer?
o: It applies automatically, because any renovation of any existing building falls under Group IX
It applies, but only at a 25% increase instead of 50%
It applies only if the PCC exceeds P50 million
It does not apply, because Group VI and Group VII buildings are outside the Groups 1-to-5 base range that Sec. 6.3.9 covers
n: Sec. 6.3.9 limits the 150%-of-RPF adjustment to alterations/renovations of buildings belonging to Groups 1 to 5. Repetitive-construction (Group VI) and housing (Group VII) buildings are governed by their own multiplier schedules (Sec. 6.3.6 / 6.3.7) and are not within the Group IX base range. Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.9

q: What is the total Group IX (150%-of-RPF) DAEDS fee for this residential renovation?
n: The Group IV DAEDS rate is a flat 10% of PCC: base RPF = 0.10 x P6,000,000 = P600,000.00. Because this is a renovation of an existing Group IV building, Sec. 6.3.9 increases it to 150%: P600,000 x 1.5 = P900,000.00. Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.4 (Group IV DAEDS fee schedule) and Sec. 6.3.9
scenario: An architect is engaged to renovate an existing single-detached residence (a Group IV building). The PCC for the renovation is PHP 6,000,000.00.

q: In JPT's ten-Group classification of Regular Design Services, where does Group IX sit, and what is it commonly labeled?
o: The sixth of ten Groups, labeled 'Repetitive Construction'
The ninth of ten Groups, labeled 'Alterations, Renovations, Rehabilitations, Retrofit, & Expansion/Addition'
The fourth of ten Groups, labeled 'Residences'
The last (tenth) Group, labeled 'Rendering of Professional Opinion'
n: The classification table lists ten Groups; Group IX (the ninth) is the one covering alterations, renovations, rehabilitations, retrofit, and expansion/addition to existing buildings, immediately after Group VIII (Extensive Detail) and before Group X (Professional Opinion). Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.9

q: What is the total Group IX (150%-of-RPF) DAEDS fee for this monumental-structure rehabilitation?
n: The Group V DAEDS rate is a flat 12% of PCC: base RPF = 0.12 x P40,000,000 = P4,800,000.00. Since this is a rehabilitation of an existing Group V building, Sec. 6.3.9 increases it to 150%: P4,800,000 x 1.5 = P7,200,000.00. Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.5 (Group V DAEDS fee schedule) and Sec. 6.3.9
scenario: An architect undertakes the restoration and rehabilitation of an existing monumental structure — a heritage mausoleum/memorial complex (a Group V – Monumental building). The PCC for the rehabilitation works is PHP 40,000,000.00.

q: An architect is engaged to design a brand-new, single-detached residence (Group IV) on a vacant lot. Should the architect apply the Group IX 150%-of-RPF adjustment to this engagement?
o: No — the Group IX adjustment applies only to alterations, renovations, rehabilitations, retrofit, or expansion/addition work on an EXISTING building, not to new construction
No — because residences are never eligible for any RPF computation
Yes — because Group IV is one of the Groups 1-to-5 eligible for the increase
Yes — all residential work automatically qualifies for the 150% Group IX rate
n: Group IX is triggered by the nature of the project (alteration/renovation/rehabilitation/retrofit/expansion of an EXISTING building), not merely by the building's base classification. A new residence built on a vacant lot is ordinary Group IV work at the standard (non-increased) RPF. Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.9

q: In the Group IX fee computations above, what does the acronym 'DAEDS' stand for?
o: Direct Architectural Estimation and Design Schedule
Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services
n: DAEDS refers to Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services — the fuller service scope (including engineering coordination) whose RPF percentages are higher than the DADS-only scope for every Group. Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3 (Regular Design Services terminology)

q: Before any Group IX adjustment, what is the ordinary (base) Group I DAEDS RPF for this project?
n: Since the PCC (P18M) is P50 million or less, the Group I DAEDS rate is a flat 5% of PCC: RPF = 0.05 x P18,000,000 = P900,000.00. Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.1 (Group I DAEDS fee schedule)
scenario: An architect is engaged for the Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services (DAEDS) of the renovation of an existing warehouse (a Group I – Simple building). The Project Construction Cost (PCC) for the renovation is PHP 18,000,000.00.

q: What does 'RPF' stand for in the context of Sec. 6.3.9's 150% rule?
n: RPF stands for Recommended Professional Fee — the fee that Sec. 6.3.9 instructs be increased to 150% for Group IX alteration/renovation work. Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.9

q: In the same warehouse-renovation scenario, how much PESO VALUE does the Group IX 50% premium itself add on top of the ordinary Group I DAEDS RPF?
n: The 50% increase (the premium alone, before adding it back to the base) is 50% of the base RPF: 0.5 x P900,000.00 = P450,000.00 (which, added to the P900,000 base, yields the P1,350,000 total 150% fee). Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.9
scenario: An architect is engaged for the Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services (DAEDS) of the renovation of an existing warehouse (a Group I – Simple building). The Project Construction Cost (PCC) for the renovation is PHP 18,000,000.00.

q: What kind of projects does Building Type Group IX cover under SPP Document 202's Regular Design Services classification?
o: New construction of monumental buildings requiring a high degree of design skill
Rendering of professional opinion or expert-witness services
Alterations, renovations, rehabilitations, retrofit, and expansion/additions to existing buildings
Repetitive construction of similar buildings using one set of plans
n: Group IX is defined as covering alterations, renovations, rehabilitations, retrofit, and expansion/additions to existing buildings — as distinguished from new construction (Groups I-V), repetitive construction (Group VI), housing projects (Group VII), extensive-detail work (Group VIII), and professional opinion (Group X). Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.9

q: Applying the Group IX rule, what is the total (150%-of-RPF) DAEDS fee the architect may charge for the hangar retrofit?
n: The base Group I DAEDS RPF is P5,100,000.00. Since this is a retrofit of an existing Group I building, Sec. 6.3.9 raises it to 150%: P5,100,000 x 1.5 = P7,650,000.00. Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.9
scenario: An architect undertakes the DAEDS renovation and structural retrofit of an existing aircraft hangar (a Group I – Simple building). The PCC for the retrofit works is PHP 120,000,000.00.

q: Which existing-building Groups may serve as the 'base Group' whose ordinary RPF is increased to 150% under the Group IX rule?
o: All ten Groups, including Group X
n: The 150%-of-RPF rule in Sec. 6.3.9 applies specifically to alterations/renovations/rehabilitations/retrofit/expansion of existing buildings 'belonging to Groups 1 to 5 enumerated above' — i.e., only buildings that would ordinarily be classified under Group I (Simple), II (Moderate), III (Exceptional), IV (Residences), or V (Monumental). Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.9

q: What is the total Group IX (150%-of-RPF) DAEDS fee for the hospital-wing addition?
n: Since PCC (P45M) is P50M or less, the Group III DAEDS rate is a flat 7% of PCC: base RPF = 0.07 x P45,000,000 = P3,150,000.00. As an addition to an existing Group III building, Sec. 6.3.9 raises this to 150%: P3,150,000 x 1.5 = P4,725,000.00. Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.3 (Group III DAEDS fee schedule) and Sec. 6.3.9
scenario: An architect is engaged for the DAEDS design of an addition of a new wing to an existing hospital (a Group III – Exceptional building). The PCC for the added wing is PHP 45,000,000.00.

q: A client asks an architect to give a professional opinion (Group X, an hourly/per-appearance fee) on whether an old building can be retrofitted. Does the Group IX 150%-of-RPF rule apply to this engagement?
o: Yes, the architect must charge 150% of the hourly rate
No, because Group X services are always rendered free of charge
Yes, because any advice concerning an existing building automatically falls under Group IX
No, because Group IX only increases the RPF of Groups 1 to 5, and Group X is compensated per hour or per appearance rather than as an RPF percentage of PCC
n: Group IX modifies the RPF of a building's base Group (limited to Groups 1-5). Group X (professional opinion) is a separate, hourly/per-appearance fee structure under Sec. 6.3.10 and is not one of the Groups 1-5 whose RPF the Group IX rule increases. Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.9
